linkedin.text:
Here's something I've seen consistently across 16 years of event production:

The destination decision is actually a messaging decision.

When a company chooses somewhere unexpected — not the obvious city, not the default resort — it signals to participants that leadership is paying attention. That signal lands before the keynote, before the agenda, before anything is said out loud.

We've seen it in groups of 50 and groups of 600. The venue choice shapes the room's energy in ways that no breakout session can manufacture.

130+ destinations later, I still think location selection is one of the most underused strategic tools in corporate events.

Curious where your industry peers are taking their teams this cycle — what destinations are you considering, and what's driving that choice?

facebook.text:
The venue doesn't just host the event — it tells the story.

When 600 people land somewhere they've never been, something shifts before the first session even starts. The unfamiliar location creates attention. The setting creates context. And suddenly your message lands differently than it would in any conference room.

We've built programs across 130+ destinations for exactly this reason.
